messages:
Alex: Quick update — I ran a short canary pass modifying the micro-batch jitter from 0.5ms -> 3ms to see if it smooths burstiness. Observed an unexpected p99 tail growth and some KV churn. Posting the basic numbers and a tiny profile dump.

Maria: Can you paste the numbers + what you changed exactly?

Alex: Sure, changed only the microbatch jitter param and coalesce_delay slightly (+0.25ms). No kernel or quant changes. Results (30s windows):
```
baseline (jitter=0.5ms, coalesce=0.5ms): p50=18ms p95=70ms p99=180ms  kv_hit=98.4%  avg_batch_size=3.2
experiment (jitter=3.0ms, coalesce=0.75ms): p50=20ms p95=85ms p99=320ms  kv_hit=96.9%  avg_batch_size=4.9
batch_size_hist: {1:34%, 2-4:48%, 5-8:14%, >8:4%}  evictions/s per node: 12 -> 46
traces: several p99s are dominated by cache-miss + kernel-switch latency (~8-12ms extra)
```
Alex: TL;DR: jitter reduced microburst noise but increased chances of larger batches that push kernel/path selection and cause KV thrash.

Sam: Interesting — did you observe any kernel selection flips? i.e., small->large-seq kernel change when batch size crosses a threshold?

Alex: No code changes in kernel selector. But runtime heuristics pick a different kernel path once batch token count > X (we see more requests grouped so token-count-per-batch crosses that cutoff more frequently). The extra path has slightly higher per-batch setup cost which amplifies on cache misses.

Kevin: My quick thought: 1) try jitter=1.0ms (middle ground), 2) enforce a soft max batch size cap (e.g., 10 requests) so we avoid kernel flip islands, 3) enable KV prefetch for hot prefixes during canary. :thumbsup:

Maria: Agreed. Can we run a small A/B tomorrow: control (jitter=0.5ms) vs two experiments (jitter=0.8ms + soft-cap=10, jitter=1.5ms + aggressive prefetch) — 2k reqs each, same traffic profile. Schedule at 11:00 UTC?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled by @Maria — env=canary-1, window=10m, start=1768561200 (11:00 UTC). Will post status.

Alex: Filed a perf regression ticket: PERF-2391. I added the traces and kernel-level counters there and linked the microbatch logs. (link: https://redwood.fake/p/PRF-2391)

Sam: If KV evictions look like the root cause, I'll prototype a lightweight hot-key priming patch that preloads top 0.5% contexts into node-local cache on detect. Should reduce miss spikes without global config churn.

Kevin: Also watch for tail latency correlation with region rack placement — if bursting batches align with node restarts we amplify misses. Add node-level timelines to the canary dashboards.

Maria: Good plan. I'll own the canary runs and metrics deck. If we still see p99 > 300ms in experiment we'll revert. Thanks team. :rocket:

Alex: Thanks — I'll attach the full trace snippets to PERF-2391 and start a short flamegraph pass on the kernel path for the bigger batches.

Sam: I'll push a prototype for KV priming to a feature branch and link it in the ticket.

Kevin: Will prepare a small perf test harness (1k qps synthetic) to stress the batch-size cutover in isolation.

Maria: Cool. Meeting after canary to review, otherwise async updates in this thread.
